title: Authority of Scripture
definition: The authority of Scripture means that the Bible speaks with the authority of God Himself. Because Scripture is God-breathed, it is the final standard for truth, doctrine, worship, obedience, correction, and discipleship.
summary: God rules His people by His Word. Scripture is not merely helpful religious writing; it carries divine authority because God has spoken. The church, the teacher, and the disciple must submit to Scripture rather than placing tradition, experience, culture, or personal opinion above it.
christFocus: Jesus Christ affirmed the authority of Scripture, fulfilled Scripture, obeyed Scripture, and taught from Scripture. To submit to the written Word is not to move away from Christ, but to listen to the Lord who reveals Himself through the Word.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Scripture has authority because God is its ultimate Author. The Bible does not borrow authority from the church, human approval, scholarship, tradition, or personal experience. It stands as the Word of God and judges all other claims.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Without the authority of Scripture, faith becomes vulnerable to personal preference, cultural pressure, false teaching, and emotional instability. The believer needs a sure foundation that does not shift when circumstances or opinions change.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple of Jesus receives Scripture with humility, tests every teaching by the Word, obeys what God has revealed, and refuses to place any human voice above the voice of God.
